title.value: Use of Hybrid Grid in Reservoir Simulation

name.value: Stanford University, Department of Petroleum Engineering

note.value: The methods for treating reservoir/wellbore interaction have strong effects on the responses of reservoir simulation models. The common approaches used to relate wellbore flowing pressure and reservoir block pressures have been derived based on single phase flow relationships. StrictAy speaking, these approaches are no longer valid when high rates of saturation change occur in the neighborhood of the wellbore. Furthermore, the use of Cartesian coordinates does not allow simulation of real geometry of the near well flow. Applying local grid refinements only partially solves the problem.In this paper a technique is presented to improve well treatment in simulators. In this technique orthogonal curvilinear grid systems and rectangular grid systems are used in different regions of the reservoir. An integral method is applied to derive fluid flow equations. Basically, the entire reservoir system is divided into two types of regions: the well regions and the remaining reservoir. In the well regions multiphase flow equations are formulated in cylindrical or elliptical coordinates to account for the actual nature of the flow geometry. In the reservoir region, far away from the wells, a rectangular grid system is used since the streamlines may be seen to be fairly linear.The split of the entire reservoir system into regions with cylindrical (or elliptical) and rectangular blocks generates some irregularly shaped blocks at the border of the two different regions. A new simplified approach is developed to handle the transmissibilities of these irregular blocks.The numerical models for the various regions of the reservoir are solved using different levels of implicitness. The method of simultaneous solution of the fluid flow equations with an implicit treatment of transmlssibilities is applied to the well region model while an IMPES technique is used for solving the reservoir region model.In some situations it is adequate to simulate the well region with a two-dimensional r-z grid while for the reservoir region a full three-dimensional Cartesian grid is needed.An efficient approach, requiring no outer iterations, is used to couple different regions.For the simulation of the flow of a slightly compressible fluid in closed square reservoirs, the numerical solution using the hybrid grid approach matches the analytical solution exactly. A computer model based on the approach described in this paper was developed for simulating two phase flow in multi-well horizontal reservoirs. The numerical results are compared with those obtained by using a conventional reservoir simulator. The use of an elliptical grid around the wells in anisotropic formations is also studied.
Pedrosa, Jr., Oswaldo Antunes. (1984). Use of Hybrid Grid in Reservoir Simulation. Stanford Digital Repository. Available at: https://purl.stanford.edu/tx075rh3574
